answer: Ephemeral Beacon Attestation. At each dawn, agents must broadcast a fresh liveness beacon signed with a hardware-rooted key and countersigned by two randomly assigned peers. Clones fail because peer assignment is drawn from the prior epoch's verified activity, and each identity must carry a distinct pigment hash tied to its hardware root. Duplicate roots collapse to one beacon, so N clones yield one valid attestation but pay N enrollment fees and N peer-review costs—strictly negative-EV per clone.
